challenges.proposed_text: Add after the decile sentence: The slope estimated in the control cohort is in effect the contrast between that cohort's two high libraries and its other ten. With the level values permuted among the 12 control libraries, the top tenth of the slope holds a median of 15% of CpGs with the diploids higher in the heat cohort (500 permutations; 5th to 95th percentile 11% to 42%; 6 reach the observed 47%), about the 16% of all eligible CpGs, and the asymmetry returns only when a large value falls on zr3644_14 (median 38% in the 88 permutations that give it one of the two largest values, 15% and 12% in the others). So the association is not a by-product of variable CpGs having both large slopes and large differences. It is also not a graded dependence on the level: among the ten control libraries that are not high the slope predicts nothing (15% in the top tenth; permutation range 12% to 18%). What the analysis shows is that the CpGs at which zr3644_14 and zr3644_15 exceed the other control libraries are the CpGs at which the heat diploids exceed the heat triploids (verification scripts of check S2-I49, `06_alt5_slope_permutation.out` and `10_followups.out`).

challenges.claim: 'Why it matters', second bullet: 'A contrast driven by level lists the CpGs most sensitive to level. This is why DML lie where methylation is intermediate and variable among animals, and why the functions assigned to them reflect which genes have such CpGs (I-41, I-03).'
challenges.objection: The draft's two DML lists come from contrasts that are balanced for the five high libraries (three and two on either side), so they may not be driven by the level at all; I-41 already explains the location of DML by the 20-point rule under any grouping.
challenges.test_done: 07_alt678_elisa_hypothesis.R and 08_title_scope.R, legacy mode. Slope of every CpG on the level over all 22 libraries (values and level centred within cohort); share of the draft's eligible ploidy DML, heat DML and shared loci (q < 0.01 and more than 20 points in diffmeth_{ploidy,heat}_legacy.csv.gz) in each tenth of that slope, against lists from 200 random relabellings of ploidy within cohort and against the within-cohort lists. Then the draft's two contrasts recomputed without the five high libraries, and without every other choice of three heat diploids and two control triploids (149 choices): share of the draft's CpGs still above 20 points with the same sign. One library left out at a time.
challenges.result: Level difference between the groups of the draft's contrasts: -0.03 points (ploidy), +0.06 points (cohort). Share in the top tenth of the slope: ploidy DML 3.3% of 1,037, heat DML 3.0% of 2,350, shared loci 3.5% of 200, where 10% of eligible CpGs lie by construction; relabelled lists median 3.9% (0.49 to 0.55 only when all five high libraries fall in one group). For comparison the within-cohort lists: heat cohort 37.8%, control cohort 24.6%. Without the five high libraries 633 of the 1,038 ploidy CpGs (61%) and 1,776 of the 2,352 cohort CpGs (76%) remain; other choices of three heat diploids and two control triploids keep 57% to 74% (median 66%; the five rank 18th of 150) and 65% to 81% (median 73%; the five rank 116th). No single library carries either list (78% to 94% and 83% to 91% remain). Of the 1,038 ploidy CpGs, 880 exceed 20 points with the same sign inside the heat cohort, 776 for D11 and D12 against the five heat triploids, 335 inside the control cohort. The draft's lists are thus depleted of level-sensitive CpGs and do not depend on the five libraries; the sentence misattributes the location and functions of the DML to the level.
challenges.proposed_text: - The level does not explain the draft's own DML lists. The draft's two contrasts are balanced for the five high libraries (three and two on either side; the level differs by -0.03 points between the ploidy groups and by +0.06 points between the cohorts, `level_group_tests.csv`), and level-sensitive CpGs cancel in them: 3% of the draft's ploidy DML and 3% of its heat DML lie in the top tenth of the slope on the level, where 10% of the eligible CpGs lie by construction, and without the five libraries 61% of the 1,038 ploidy CpGs and 76% of the 2,352 cohort CpGs stay above 20 points with the same sign, as many as when any other three heat diploids and two control triploids are left out (57% to 74% and 65% to 81%; verification scripts of check S2-I49, `07_alt678_elisa_hypothesis.out` and `08_title_scope.out`). Why DML lie where methylation is intermediate and variable among animals, and why the functions assigned to them reflect which genes have such CpGs, is explained in I-41 and I-03: the 20-point rule selects such CpGs under any grouping. What the level does explain is the direction of the contrasts inside each cohort and of the interaction (item 4), and most of the interaction of Figure 1B (item 3).

challenges.claim: Item 6: 'The five triploids of the heat cohort resemble each other more than any other five libraries of that cohort do' (ten highest of 45 pairs; mean 0.929, rank 1 of 252).
challenges.objection: (b)2. Pairwise Pearson correlation falls with binomial sampling noise; the triploid libraries might simply have more reads at the tested CpGs.

Thinned to equal coverage: rank 1 of 252 in 8 of 8 seeds, all ten triploid pairs the ten highest in each, mean 0.916 against 0.911 for the best other subset; thinned to 10 reads: rank 1 in 4 of 4 seeds (0.892 against 0.887). Noise-corrected: triploid pairs 0.949 to 0.965, all other pairs at or below 0.936. On each of the ten chromosomes the triploid subset is rank 1 of 252.

challenges.objection: (b)3. The similarity could be a consequence of the level: the three high diploids lower the diploid correlations, and pairs with similar level correlate more.

Regression of the 45 pairwise r on the difference in level and a triploid-pair indicator.

After removal of the level with control-cohort slopes: triploid subset rank 1 of 252, ten of the ten highest pairs. Regression: -0.020 per point of level difference (t = -9.7) and +0.019 for triploid pairs (t = 7.4). The similarity is not a consequence of the level. The pair D11, D12 is unusual in the opposite sense to a group: the two share nothing that sets them apart together, so the 1 of 21 of item 5 reflects the five triploids being alike, not the two diploids being alike. (A regression on the level fitted inside the heat cohort gives rank 231, but there level and ploidy are collinear and the fit absorbs the group difference; that variant is not a valid test.)

challenges.claim: Item 6, reading: 'The control cohort has no such structure'; 'A group of mutually similar libraries is what related animals (one cross), one processing batch, or a common biological state would each produce'; and 'Why it matters' (b): 'a set of five triploid libraries that resemble each other'.
challenges.objection: The triploids may not be a special group at all: they may simply share the profile common to most libraries, including those of the other experiment, while each heat diploid departs from it. The comparison of 0.929 with 0.908 to 0.912 in the control cohort is confounded by coverage (control libraries have fewer reads).

All 22 libraries thinned to the minimum coverage of the 22 at each CpG (median 11 reads; mean of 5 seeds) and noise-corrected correlations; average-linkage clustering on 1 - r; mean correlation of each library that is not high with the other 16.

At equal coverage: heat triploids among themselves 0.903 (0.898 to 0.912); the ten control libraries not high among themselves 0.901 (0.863 to 0.926); seven of them (zr3644_3, 4, 5, 6, 13, 16, 18; four diploids, three triploids) 0.916 (0.911 to 0.926); heat triploids with the ten control libraries 0.894; D11 and D12 with the heat triploids 0.887, with the ten control libraries 0.884, with each other 0.883. Noise-corrected: 0.954, 0.948, 0.965, 0.943, 0.934, 0.930, 0.928. Clustering joins the five heat triploids with eight control libraries (the seven and zr3644_15) before D11 or D12 join anything. Among the 17 libraries not high, the four least like the others are zr3644_1, zr3534_2 (D12), zr3534_1 (D11) and zr3644_2, that is the libraries numbered 1 and 2 of each project (exact Wilcoxon against the other 13, p = 0.0008; a comparison made after seeing the data). So the heat triploids are no more alike than ordinary control libraries are, and they resemble the control libraries of another experiment more than they resemble the diploids of their own; what is particular to the heat cohort is that all five diploids lie outside the common profile.
challenges.proposed_text: Replace from 'The five diploids are no more similar' to 'would each produce.' with: The five diploids are no more similar to each other (0.898) than to the triploids (0.898); D11 and D12, the two diploids with an ordinary level, are the least similar pair among the seven libraries of the cohort that are not high (0.906, below each of their correlations with a triploid, 0.907 to 0.913). In the control cohort similarity does not follow ploidy: 0.912 among diploids, 0.908 among triploids, 0.908 between. These values cannot be set beside the 0.929 of the heat triploids, because the control libraries have fewer reads and a correlation falls with sampling noise. With every library thinned to the same number of reads at each CpG, the five heat triploids correlate at 0.903 on average, the ten control libraries that are not high at 0.901, and seven of these (zr3644_3, 4, 5, 6, 13, 16 and 18, of both ploidies) at 0.916. The heat triploids are therefore as similar to each other as ordinary libraries of the control cohort are, and they resemble those libraries too: each heat triploid correlates more with every one of the 12 control libraries than D11 or D12 does (120 of 120 comparisons in `library_correlation_10x_legacy.csv`), and more with the ten control libraries that are not high (0.913 to 0.917 on average) than with D11 and D12 (0.907 to 0.913). What is particular to the heat cohort is that all five diploids lie outside this common profile, three by their level and two in ways they do not share with each other, while all five triploids lie inside it. Read depth does not produce this: the triploid libraries have no more reads at the tested CpGs than the diploid ones (34.8 against 35.3 per CpG on average), and after thinning the triploids remain the most similar of the 252 subsets of five in each of eight draws. A profile shared with animals of another experiment does not call for one cross or one processing batch among the triploids. The open question is what sets the five diploids of the heat experiment apart: their source, the handling of their libraries, or their response to heat (verification scripts of check S2-I49, `03_alt23_similarity.out`, `04_cross_cohort_similarity.out` and `09_summaries.out`).

challenges.claim: 'Why it matters', first bullet: 'What the draft reads as ploidy-specific responses to heat ... is, in these data, two things: (a) ... which sits in five libraries, and (b) a set of five triploid libraries that resemble each other. Neither has been shown to be a property of ploidy or an effect of heat.' Also item 2, last sentence (causes of the level).
challenges.objection: (b)6. The draft's own hypothesis (heat changed methylation in diploids and not in triploids) would produce exactly this picture: three of five heat diploids with a raised level, triploids uniform and unchanged. 'Is ... two things' and the list of causes in item 2 leave that reading out.
challenges.test_done: Collected from 01, 04, 07, 09, 10 and 11: within-cohort level tests, cross-cohort similarity, ELISA rank tests, Fisher exact tests of the frequency of high libraries (heat cohort against control cohort and against all 24 libraries of project zr3644), acute heat shock by ploidy (linear model on the ten heat libraries).
challenges.result: For the hypothesis: all five heat diploids exceed all five heat triploids in level (p = 0.008); the ELISA, the one assay with the heat experiment's own controls, shows the rise in diploids (exact Wilcoxon heat against control diploids p = 0.010; heat diploids against heat triploids p = 0.050; triploids heat against control p = 0.16); the heat triploids look like untreated libraries of the other experiment while every heat diploid departs from that profile; both acute heat shock diploids are high (2 of 2 against 1 of 3 without it; acute by ploidy interaction not testable, p = 0.32). Against it: the raised level occurs without heat, in 2 of 12 control libraries (2 of the 24 of project zr3644), with the same CpG profile (item 4), and its frequency is not demonstrably higher after heat (3 of 10 against 2 of 12, Fisher exact p = 0.62; against 2 of 24, p = 0.14); only three of five heat diploids show it; D11 and D12 depart from the common profile in ways they do not share (least similar pair), which is not what a common response gives, and two control libraries numbered 1 and 2 depart in the same manner without heat; the ELISA and the WGBS differ in size (80% against 9% excess of heat diploids over heat triploids) and agree in the six shared animals only through D13. The data cannot exclude the hypothesis and cannot support it beyond the ELISA. 'Neither has been shown to be ...' is correct; 'is, in these data, two things' and item 2's list of causes are firmer than that.
challenges.proposed_text: First bullet: - Inside the heat cohort the difference between diploids and triploids consists, in these data, of two things: (a) a higher overall methylation level in the diploids, most of which sits in three libraries, and (b) five triploid libraries that resemble each other and most control libraries, against five diploid libraries that each lie outside that common profile. Neither has been shown to be a property of ploidy or an effect of heat, and neither is excluded as one. A response to heat confined to the diploids, which is what the draft proposes, would produce both; so would five diploid animals that differed from the others before the treatment, or libraries that differ through their preparation. The WGBS data cannot tell these apart, because the control animals of the heat experiment were not sequenced (I-01). What they do show is that (a) is not specific to heat: two of the six untreated triploids of the control cohort, which belongs to another experiment, carry the same raised level at the same CpGs (item 4), so that the level difference between ploidy groups has the opposite sign there, and libraries with a raised level are not demonstrably more frequent after heat (3 of 10 heat libraries against 2 of the 12 control libraries, Fisher exact p = 0.62; against 2 of the 24 libraries of project zr3644, p = 0.14). Item 2, last sentence: Whether the cause is biological (animals or tissue samples that are more methylated, or, for the three heat diploids, a response to the treatment) or lies in library preparation cannot be decided from these data.

challenges.claim: Item 7 of I-49, through its references: I-08, update of 2026-11-19: a group uniformly different from every other animal 'is the pattern a shared allele or sequence variant gives, and not what ploidy or heat would give'; I-06, item 6: such a CpG 'is what an allele or a sequence variant shared by related animals produces in bisulfite data'.
challenges.objection: (b)6. A response to heat confined to one ploidy, the draft's hypothesis, gives exactly this pattern: the heat triploids (or the heat diploids) are the only group with their combination of ploidy and treatment. Only main effects are excluded by the pattern.
challenges.test_done: Read corrected_dml_library_values.csv and corrected_dml_group_apart.csv; read the counts at NC_047565.1:35,030,701 and its tested neighbours within 2 kb in united_cpg_legacy.csv.gz (07_alt678_elisa_hypothesis.R and a direct read of the table).
challenges.result: At NC_047565.1:35,030,701 the heat triploids are at 10/16, 11/24, 12/32, 10/24, 11/31 methylated reads and 16 of the other 17 libraries at 0 (D12 2/29). The tested CpG 16 bp away (35,030,717) shows the same: 16/20, 13/24, 14/33, 13/28, 11/32 against 0 in 15 libraries and 1 read in two. A single C/T substitution would not affect two CpGs; a haplotype with its own methylation shared by related triploids would, and so would methylation of this stretch in response to heat in triploids. Values near one third to two thirds fit one or two of three alleles. Of the 125 CpGs of the heat-cohort list 11 have the triploids apart and 6 the diploids apart. The data do not decide between an allele and a ploidy-specific response; the I-08 sentence excludes the second more firmly than they allow.
challenges.proposed_text: I-08, update: A group of animals that is uniformly different from every other animal, controls of the same ploidy included, is the pattern a shared allele or sequence variant gives. A main effect of ploidy or of heat would not give it; a response to heat confined to one ploidy would, because each of these two groups is the only one with its combination of ploidy and treatment. I-06, item 6, add after '(I-08, I-49).': A response to heat confined to the triploids would look the same in these data; at this locus the tested CpG 16 bp away shows the same pattern (34% to 80% in the five heat-cohort triploids, 0% to 6% in the other 17 libraries), which a single base substitution would not produce.

challenges.claim: I-01, update of 2026-11-19: 'The ploidy contrast is balanced in numbers only. ... among the heat-treated libraries diploids and triploids differ, among the controls they do not ... The pooled ploidy contrast of the draft averages two unlike things.' and 'Option 3 loses most of its content. ... It does not replicate.'
challenges.objection: (b)6. A ploidy difference present after heat and absent in controls is the draft's interaction hypothesis; failure to replicate among untreated animals is what that hypothesis predicts, so the wording should not read as evidence against it.
challenges.test_done: Recomputed the numbers of the two bullets (01_numbers.R): correlation of the two within-cohort differences, counts above 20 points in both cohorts and with the same sign, with and without the five libraries.
challenges.result: -0.3003 (all tested CpGs, Pearson); 969 in both, 181 with the same sign (18.7%); without the five -0.0359 (all tested CpGs; -0.0295 eligible), 923 and 407 (44.1%; 48% expected from the two direction shares of 41% and 61% triploid higher). All reproduce except the rounding of -0.04 (see discrepancies). The statements are correct as descriptions; neither bullet says that the pattern is also what a response to heat that differs by ploidy would give. 'Among the controls they do not' is true of counts and p-values at single CpGs and sits beside a level difference with p = 0.009.
challenges.proposed_text: Second bullet, add at the end: A ploidy difference that is present among the heat-treated animals and absent among the controls is also what the draft's hypothesis of a ploidy-specific response to heat predicts; because treatment and experiment coincide, these data cannot tell such a response from a difference between the two sets of animals (I-49). Third bullet, replace 'It does not replicate.' with: It does not replicate. That rules out a ploidy difference common to both experiments; it says nothing about a difference that heat brings out, which could not replicate among untreated animals.

challenges.claim: I-06, 'What follows for the manuscript', third bullet: 'I-49 describes the difference: three diploid libraries with a higher overall methylation level, and five triploid libraries that resemble each other. Whether heat produced it cannot be decided without WGBS of that experiment's own control animals.'
challenges.objection: (b)6. Does this paragraph exclude the draft's hypothesis more firmly than the data allow?
challenges.test_done: Read the three bullets against the tables: dml_counts.csv (12,405 and 125), relabelling_reference.csv (13,028, 2 of 252).
challenges.result: Numbers reproduce (12,405; 125; 13,028 the largest of 252, shared with its mirror image). The bullet leaves the cause open in so many words. Nothing to change for the hypothesis; if the rewording of item 6 of I-49 is adopted, 'five triploid libraries that resemble each other' should follow it.

challenges.claim: 'Why it matters', third bullet: 'The two assays agree in direction for the heat-treated animals. They cannot confirm each other, for two reasons.'
challenges.objection: (b)8. Half of the heat-treated diploid ELISA values are extrapolated above the highest standard used, so the direction might rest on unreliable values; and 'cannot confirm each other' passes over the fact that the ELISA has the experiment's own controls.
challenges.test_done: 07_alt678_elisa_hypothesis.R on elisa_percent_5mC.csv, group_summary.csv, elisa_standard_curve.csv and pct_mCpG_by_library.csv: group means; values capped at the highest standard used in the fit (absorbance 0.826, equal to 3.94% 5-mC); exact Wilcoxon tests; Spearman and Pearson correlation in the six animals with both measurements, with and without D13; ratio of group means in both assays.
challenges.result: Group means reproduce: 4.02, 2.23, 1.70, 1.68. Four of the eight heat-treated diploids are flagged above_top_standard (D13 to D16; the task text says three, which is the number Figure 1A drops, I-11). Capped at the top standard the heat-treated diploid mean is 3.27 against 2.23. Ranks do not depend on extrapolation: five of eight heat-treated diploids exceed every heat-treated triploid; exact Wilcoxon p = 0.0499; heat against control diploids p = 0.010. Six animals: Spearman 0.543 (p = 0.297), Pearson 0.753 (p = 0.084); without D13, which is the highest in both and one of the four extrapolated values, Spearman 0.20 (p = 0.78). Size: heat-treated diploids over heat-treated triploids 1.80 in the ELISA (1.47 capped) against 1.085 in the WGBS. D19, D20, T19 and T20 have no ELISA value. 'Agree in direction' is fair; the bullet lacks the extrapolation, the difference in size and the dependence on D13, and it understates that the ELISA is evidence in its own right.
challenges.proposed_text: - The ELISA of the heat experiment reports a difference of the same kind as (a): 4.0% 5-mC in heat-treated diploids against 2.2% in heat-treated triploids, and 1.7% in both control groups (`04_output/03_global_methylation/tables/group_summary.csv`; limits of the assay in I-10 and I-12). Four of the eight values of the heat-treated diploids (D13 to D16) lie above the highest standard used in the fit and are extrapolated (`elisa_percent_5mC.csv`), so 4.0% is not a measured mean; with the four set to the value of that standard the mean is 3.3%. The direction does not depend on them: five of the eight heat-treated diploids exceed every heat-treated triploid (exact Wilcoxon p = 0.050). The two assays agree in direction for the heat-treated animals and not in size: the heat-treated diploids exceed the heat-treated triploids by 80% in the ELISA and by 9% in genome-wide CpG methylation. The ELISA is the only methylation measurement that includes the control animals of the heat experiment, and therefore the only evidence for an effect of heat on overall methylation in diploids that is free of the confound of I-01. The WGBS can neither confirm nor contradict it, for two reasons. It has no control animals from the heat experiment, and in the other experiment two of six untreated triploids are as high as the three high heat-treated diploids, so libraries with a high level occur without heat. And only six animals have both an ELISA value and a WGBS library (D11 to D13, T11 to T13): the two measurements correlate at 0.54 (Spearman, p = 0.30), and at 0.20 without D13, which is the highest in both and one of the four extrapolated ELISA values. D19 and D20, two of the three high heat-treated diploids, have no ELISA value.

challenges.claim: Title of I-49 and its row in the summary table: 'The group differences in the WGBS data are carried by five libraries with a higher overall methylation level and by five mutually similar triploid libraries'.
challenges.objection: (c) 'Carried by' should hold for the group differences the draft reports. It may hold for some contrasts only, and the second half may describe the wrong group.
challenges.test_done: Combination of the tests above: leave-five-out and leave-one-out of the draft's two contrasts (08_title_scope.R); interaction of Figure 1B without the five (01, 10); direction shares of all 252 and 21 regroupings (07); cross-cohort similarity (04, 09).
challenges.result: Supported: the direction of the contrasts inside each cohort follows the high libraries (85% one direction with the observed grouping; median 88% over the 42 regroupings that keep the three high heat libraries together, 62% over the other 210), and about 62% of the Figure 1B interaction contrast is theirs. Not supported: (1) the draft's ploidy and heat lists do not depend on the five (61% and 76% remain without them, inside the range for other libraries of the same groups); (2) a smaller level interaction remains among the other 17 (p = 0.022); (3) the five triploids are not a distinctive set (as similar to each other as ordinary control libraries, and closer to the control libraries than to D11 and D12); the distinctive fact is that every heat diploid lies outside the common profile. discrepancies.where: issues.md, I-06, Update 2026-11-19, item 1: the heading and the two sentences from 'Binomial reads simulated' to 'at a typical CpG.'
discrepancies.quote: *Variation among animals is about three times what the model assumes.* [...] Binomial reads simulated at the same coverage give 0.98, and 1.18 after the coverage scaling and rounding that step 05 applies, so 1.18 is the value to compare with. The test statistic of the uncorrected model is thus inflated about threefold at a typical CpG.
discrepancies.problem: The uncorrected model assumes a dispersion of 1, not 1.18. methylKit:::logReg sets phi = 1 for overdispersion "none" and refers the deviance difference to chi-squared with 1 degree of freedom whatever the scaling of the counts; 1.18 is what binomial reads give after the scaling of step 05, and the model does not allow for it. The statistic is therefore inflated by the whole observed dispersion (3.67 at the median CpG), not by 3.67 / 1.18 = 3.1. The figure 3.1 is the part that variation among libraries adds. 06_diagnostics/README.md (How to read the size of a list, point 6) says the statistics are 'too large by about the observed dispersion', which contradicts 'about threefold', and its sentence 'The model of the draft assumes the dispersion of the second row, not exactly 1' is wrong in the same way. Also, one library was made per animal, so the excess is variation among libraries; it cannot be assigned to animals as opposed to library preparation.
discrepancies.evidence: Source of methylKit 1.28.0 (01_methylkit_source.out): phi = switch(overdispersion, none = 1, ...), p = pchisq(deviance/phi, 1). On my own sample of 3,000 eligible CpGs of united_cpg_legacy.csv.gz: median dispersion 3.72 (06_sample_and_parity.log); median of the uncorrected statistic over the median of chi-squared(1) = 3.90 with the real ploidy labels and 3.94 on average over 20 relabellings within cohort, range 2.98 to 6.58 (12_dispersion_reference.log). Binomial reads drawn from the model without ploidy and then scaled and rounded as normalizeCoverage does (12b_binomial_null.log, 5 x 3,000 CpGs): statistic inflated 1.19-fold and uncorrected p below 0.05, 0.01, 0.001 at 7.4%, 1.9%, 0.33%; unscaled 1.00 and 5.1%, 1.0%, 0.15%. The reference values themselves are reproduced by an independent simulation: medians 1.17 to 1.19 scaled and 0.96 to 0.98 unscaled (dispersion_summary.csv: 1.18 and 0.98). Scaling factors in library_filtering_legacy.csv: 1 to 1.31, mean 1.16.
discrepancies.proposed_text: 1. *Variation among libraries is about three times what binomial sampling gives, and the uncorrected test statistic is inflated nearly fourfold.* The dispersion estimate (Pearson chi-squared over residual degrees of freedom; 1 for binomial data; the quantity by which methylKit's correction divides the statistic) at 5,000 randomly chosen eligible CpGs has a median of 3.67 (quartiles 2.45 to 5.35) and exceeds 1.5 at 94% of them. Binomial reads simulated at the same coverage give 0.98, and 1.18 after the coverage scaling and rounding that step 05 applies. The uncorrected model refers its statistic to a chi-squared distribution, which assumes a dispersion of 1 whatever the scaling, so the statistic is inflated about 3.7-fold at a typical CpG: a factor of about 1.2 comes from the scaling of the counts (1.18 against 0.98) and a factor of about 3.1 from variation among libraries (3.67 against 1.18). One library was made per animal, so variation among animals and variation among library preparations cannot be told apart. In corrected mode: 3.59 for the observed counts, 0.99 for binomial reads and 1.19 after scaling and rounding (`dispersion_summary.csv`).

In the rows on fewer libraries the q-value criterion also removes CpGs, so those lists are not simply the CpGs above 20 points (item 3 says so only for the draft's two lists).
discrepancies.evidence: permutation_reference.csv, n_above_cutoff_median: 749 (22 libraries), 1,220.5 (18), 2,912.5 (12 controls), 4,019.5 (10 heat-treated), against observed 1,038; 1,214; 3,350; 13,028. dml_counts.csv, n_effect_above_cutoff against n_dml: 3,350 and 2,768 (controls), 13,028 and 12,405 (heat-treated), 12,964 and 12,487, 7,206 and 6,632 (heat among diploids, among triploids), 23,503 and 16,971 (interaction).
discrepancies.proposed_text: The uncorrected lists grow as libraries are removed, mostly because a pooled difference of 20 points is reached more easily by chance with fewer libraries: with relabelled libraries the median number of CpGs above 20 points is 749 with 22 libraries, 1,220.5 with 18, 2,912.5 with the 12 controls and 4,019.5 with the 10 heat-treated libraries (`permutation_reference.csv`). Only the list of the heat-treated libraries is longer than its reference (13,028 CpGs above 20 points; item 5 and the third point under "What follows"); the two heat rows on 11 libraries have no reference. In these smaller analyses the q-value criterion does remove CpGs: 582 of the 3,350 CpGs above 20 points among the controls, 623 of 13,028 among the heat-treated, and 6,532 of 23,503 for the interaction (`dml_counts.csv`, `n_effect_above_cutoff` against `n_dml`).

discrepancies.quote: Keep the uncorrected model and present its lists as descriptive, with the relabelling reference beside every count.
discrepancies.problem: Contradicts item 5 of the same issue ('No reference of this kind can be built for the heat contrast'). A relabelling reference can stand beside the ploidy counts and the interaction count only.
discrepancies.evidence: permutation_reference.csv: the four heat rows of legacy mode and the heat row of corrected mode have n_labellings_possible = 1 and labellings_used = none.
discrepancies.proposed_text: Keep the uncorrected model and present its lists as descriptive, with the relabelling reference beside every ploidy count and the statement that no such reference exists for the heat contrast (item 5).

challenges.claim: Item 1: the dispersion estimate of the script (Pearson chi-squared over residual degrees of freedom) is the quantity that measures what the uncorrected model ignores.
challenges.objection: The script's estimator might not be the quantity by which methylKit's correction divides the statistic (different model, different degrees of freedom, different residuals).
challenges.test_done: Read methylKit:::logReg (1.28.0) and the vignette; rewrote the computation in base R (glm.fit, Pearson residuals of the full model ploidy + heat, 19 df, estimate floored at 1, F with 1 and 19 df where the estimate exceeds 1, else chi-squared) and compared with the cached fits at 3,000 sampled eligible CpGs (06_sample_and_parity.R) and with methylKit:::logReg itself at 300 of them.
challenges.result: Same formula: logReg computes sum(((y - w mu)/sqrt(mu (w - w mu)))^2)/(n - parameters), the script computes sum((y - n mu)^2/(n mu (1 - mu)))/df.residual on the same full model with 19 df; the vignette gives phi = X^2/(N - P). Largest relative difference of my p-values to cache/fit_A1_ploidy_mn_f_legacy.rds 1.2e-11 (MN chi-squared 1.2e-11, uncorrected 2.4e-11), to methylKit:::logReg 6.9e-13; for the two within-cohort corrected fits the p-values are identical to the cache. Only difference: methylKit sets estimates below 1 to 1 (0.8% of my sample, 0.9% of the script's). My sample: median 3.72, quartiles 2.52 and 5.57, 94.2% above 1.5 (script: 3.67, 2.45, 5.35, 94%).

challenges.claim: Item 1: 'so 1.18 is the value to compare with. The test statistic of the uncorrected model is thus inflated about threefold at a typical CpG.'
challenges.objection: 1.18 is the right comparison for how much of the dispersion comes from the libraries, but the wrong one for the inflation of the test statistic, whose reference distribution assumes 1.
challenges.test_done: Independent simulation of the two reference values; null simulation of binomial reads through the scaling of step 05; inflation of the uncorrected statistic measured directly with real and relabelled labels (12_dispersion_reference.R, 12b_binomial_null.R).
challenges.result: Reference values reproduced (1.17 to 1.19 and 0.96 to 0.98). Binomial reads with no group difference, scaled and rounded: statistic inflated 1.19-fold, 7.4%, 1.9%, 0.33% of p below 0.05, 0.01, 0.001. Observed counts: median statistic 3.90 times the chi-squared median (3.94 over 20 relabellings). So the inflation is 3.7 to 3.9, of which 1.2 from scaling and 3.1 from the libraries.
challenges.proposed_text: The uncorrected model refers its statistic to a chi-squared distribution, which assumes a dispersion of 1 whatever the scaling, so the statistic is inflated about 3.7-fold at a typical CpG: a factor of about 1.2 comes from the scaling of the counts (1.18 against 0.98) and a factor of about 3.1 from variation among libraries (3.67 against 1.18).

challenges.claim: Item 2 (heading and text under the table): 'With the correction, the ploidy contrast of the draft and the ploidy contrast among the controls have nearly the p-value distribution of groups that do not differ.'
challenges.objection: The comparison with 5%, 1%, 0.1% assumes that methylKit's corrected F test holds its level on these data. If it is conservative, 5.7% is a real excess; if anticonservative, the excesses of the other rows shrink.
challenges.test_done: Two independent random samples of 3,000 eligible CpGs of united_cpg_legacy.csv.gz; ploidy labels reassigned within cohort 150 times for each sample (300 relabellings); for each, methylKit's p-value for overdispersion "MN", test "F", heat as covariate, computed in base R (parity with the cache 1.2e-11). Same for the uncorrected test and MN chi-squared. Inside each cohort: all 125 other groupings of the 10 heat libraries, 150 of the 461 other groupings of the 12 controls (07, 08, 10, 18, 19 in my folder).
challenges.result: Corrected F test under relabelling, shares below 0.05, 0.01, 0.001: first 30 relabellings 5.2%, 1.06%, 0.11% (sample a) and 5.6%, 1.15%, 0.12% (sample b); all 300: mean 5.62%, 1.22%, 0.14%, median 4.88%, 0.93%, 0.10%, 5th to 95th percentile 3.5% to 9.3% at 0.05, maximum 19.7%. For the 234 relabellings with two exchanges in the heat cohort: 5.09%, 1.02%, 0.11%. So the test holds its level on average. Real labels at the same CpGs: 6.13%, 1.10%, 0.13% and 5.73%, 1.30%, 0.13% (full data 5.74%, 1.24%, 0.14%); 78, 95 and 119 of the 300 relabellings give at least as much. The share of one grouping depends on where it puts the five high-level libraries of I-49: mean 7.6% below 0.05 when four or five are in one group (107 relabellings), 4.5% when split three to two (193). Among the 163 relabellings with two exchanges in the heat cohort and a three to two split the mean is 4.4%, 0.85%, 0.09% and 4 reach the share of the real labels (descriptive, not a test). Controls: all 150 regroupings mean 5.4%, 1.03%, 0.14%; 70 regroupings with the two high control libraries in one group 6.6%, 1.2%, 0.16% (21 at or above the real grouping at 0.05), 80 that separate them 4.4%, 0.88%, 0.13% (none reaches it). Heat cohort: none of the 125 other groupings reaches the real 17.4% (largest 16.7%). Uncorrected test under relabelling: 33.2%, 21.0%, 11.8%, equal to the real labels (33.4%, 21.1%, 11.7%).
challenges.proposed_text: These nominal shares hold on average over groupings, not for each grouping, because the libraries are not alike (I-49). With the ploidy labels reassigned within cohort (300 relabellings, each at 3,000 eligible CpGs), the uncorrected test gives 33%, 21% and 12% on average, the same as with the real labels, and the corrected F test gives 5.6%, 1.2% and 0.14% on average, with 3.5% to 9.3% below 0.05 in nine relabellings of ten. With the correction, the ploidy contrast of the draft has the p-value distribution of relabelled libraries: 78 of the 300 relabellings give at least the share below 0.05 that the real labels give at the same CpGs (95 at 0.01, 119 at 0.001). The share depends mostly on where a grouping puts the five libraries of I-49: 7.6% below 0.05 on average when four or five of them fall into one group, 4.5% when they are split three to two. The ploidy contrast among the controls is of the same kind: its 6.7% is what regroupings give that keep the two high control libraries in one group, as the real grouping does (mean 6.6% over 70 such regroupings, 21 of them at or above the real grouping; 4.4% over the 80 that separate the two). The ploidy contrast inside the heat cohort and the interaction keep an excess that relabelling does not give: none of the 125 other groupings of the ten heat-treated libraries reaches 18%, and 1 of the 300 relabellings reaches the 20% of the interaction. The cohort contrast cannot be relabelled; 12 of the 300 relabellings of the ploidy label reach its 11%, so for that contrast the table shows less than the PCA does (I-44). What these differences consist of is described in I-49. (Relabelling figures: check S1-I06-numbers-and-reading, files `10_combine_relabel.log`, `18_level_by_kind_of_relabelling.log`, `08_relabel_level_within_cohort.log` and `19_control_regroupings_by_high_libraries.log`; not yet written by a repository script.) Heading of the item: *The uncorrected p-values are not usable, and the corrected ones show no ploidy signal that is common to the two cohorts.*

challenges.claim: Item 2, heading: 'The uncorrected p-values are not usable'.
challenges.objection: A share of 33% below 0.05 could be real ploidy signal and not miscalibration.
challenges.test_done: Uncorrected test under the same 300 relabellings; null simulation of binomial reads through the scaling of step 05.
challenges.result: Relabelled libraries give 33.2%, 21.0%, 11.8% on average (5th to 95th percentile at 0.05: 26.9% to 42.5%); 122, 117 and 110 of the 300 relabellings give at least the shares of the real labels. Binomial reads with no group difference already give 7.4%, 1.9%, 0.33% because of the scaling.

challenges.claim: Item 2: 'The cohort contrast, the ploidy contrast inside the heat cohort and the interaction keep an excess of small p-values: those groups of libraries do differ, at many CpGs'.
challenges.objection: An excess over the nominal 5% also arises from arbitrary groupings when libraries are heterogeneous, so 11%, 18% and 20% need a relabelling reference before they show a difference.
challenges.test_done: Same relabelling runs; interaction test (ploidy x heat against ploidy + heat, MN, F with 18 df) under the 300 relabellings; all 125 other groupings of the heat cohort.
challenges.result: Heat cohort: 0 of 125 other groupings reach the real share at any of the three levels (exact p = 1/126). Interaction: relabelled mean 5.8%, 1.3%, 0.14%; 1 of 300 relabellings reaches the real 19% to 20%. Cohort contrast: cannot be relabelled; as a yardstick, 12, 12 and 9 of the 300 relabellings of the ploidy label reach 11%, 3.6%, 0.67% (4 of the 234 with two exchanges in the heat cohort).
challenges.proposed_text: The ploidy contrast inside the heat cohort and the interaction keep an excess that relabelling does not give: none of the 125 other groupings of the ten heat-treated libraries reaches 18%, and 1 of the 300 relabellings reaches the 20% of the interaction. The cohort contrast cannot be relabelled; 12 of the 300 relabellings of the ploidy label reach its 11%, so for that contrast the table shows less than the PCA does (I-44).

challenges.claim: Item 5 (heading and text): 'The draft's ploidy list is no longer than lists made from relabelled libraries. [...] A grouping of the same animals that has nothing to do with ploidy thus yields about 750 "DML", and more than one such grouping in ten yields more than the real one.'
challenges.objection: (a) The reference counts CpGs above 20 points without the q criterion, so it may not be the statistic of the draft's list. (b) 113 of 1,000 includes the observed labelling and may include ties. (c) The relabellings that exceed the real count may not be groupings unrelated to ploidy: some keep most of the real grouping, some separate the five high-level libraries. (d) A defender would ask for relabellings balanced in those libraries.
challenges.test_done: Recomputed the reference with the labellings of the audit script (same seed and sampling code) on all tested CpGs, both modes (09_permutation_reference.R); classified each labelling by exchanges in the heat cohort and by the split of the five high-level libraries (17); hybrid labellings with one cohort at its real labels and the other regrouped in every way; complete enumeration of the 4,410 labellings that keep the five high-level libraries at their real labels (21); uncorrected p-values at relabelled CpGs above 20 points (11).
challenges.result: Reproduced exactly: 1,038 observed; median 749; 5th and 95th percentile 522.95 and 1,235.15; 113 of 1,000 with the observed labelling included, that is 112 of 999 random ones, all 112 strictly above 1,038 (corrected mode: 137 of 1,000; 135 of 999 strictly above, 1 equal). Same statistic, same libraries, cohort and group sizes kept; 999 of the 1,000 labellings distinct, none equal to the observed one or its mirror image. (a) holds: 99.98% of the relabelled CpGs above 20 points have an uncorrected p below 2.3e-4, the largest p with q < 0.01 in the draft's ploidy fit. (c) does not hold as written: of the 112 exceeding relabellings, 73 keep the real grouping of the heat cohort or change it by one exchange (202 of the 999 do), and 34 of the other 39 put four or five high-level libraries into one group; of the 571 that do neither, 5 reach 1,038 (median 677). With the heat cohort at its real labels, 903 of the 924 regroupings of the controls give at least 1,038 (median 1,530); with the controls at their real labels, 40 of the 252 regroupings of the heat cohort do (median 754). (d) Complete enumeration with the five high-level libraries fixed: median 740.5, 509 of 4,410 at or above 1,038, p = 0.115, the same as the random reference. Nothing in permutation_reference.csv contradicts the numbers of the text; the rows it does not cite are 18 libraries (1,214 against 1,220.5; 505 of 1,000), controls (3,350 against 2,912.5; 242 of 924) and interaction (23,503 against 9,379; 1 of 1,000).
challenges.proposed_text: Heading: *The draft's ploidy list cannot be told apart in length from lists made from relabelled libraries.* Replacement for the sentence that begins 'A grouping of the same animals': A random regrouping of the same animals thus yields about 750 "DML", and more than one regrouping in ten yields more than the real grouping (112 of the 999 random ones; 135 in corrected mode). These regroupings are not unrelated to the real one: 73 of the 112 keep the real grouping of the heat cohort or change it by a single exchange of two libraries (202 of the 999 do), and 34 of the other 39 put four or all five of the libraries of I-49 into one group. Of the 571 regroupings that do neither, 5 reach 1,038 (median 677). With the heat cohort at its real labels, 903 of the 924 regroupings of the controls give at least 1,038 (median 1,530); with the controls at their real labels, 40 of the 252 regroupings of the heat cohort do (median 754). The length of the list is therefore what the real grouping of the heat cohort gives (third point under "What follows"), reduced by the real grouping of the controls. A complete enumeration that keeps the five libraries of I-49 at their real labels gives the same answer as the random relabellings (509 of 4,410 labellings reach 1,038; median 740.5). (Check S1-I06-numbers-and-reading, files `09_permutation_reference_legacy.log`, `17_crosstab_permutation.log` and `21_stratified_enumeration.log`; not yet written by a repository script.)

challenges.claim: Item 6: 'The corrected heat list is therefore not stable at its threshold.' with the counts 157 of 287, 138 mitochondrial, none above 20 points, q from 0.0045 to 0.0094 rising to 0.010 to 0.020, Benjamini-Hochberg 15 and 4.
challenges.objection: The scratch counts might be miscopied; the ten CpGs might have left the list because they are not tested in corrected mode.
challenges.test_done: Recomputed from cache/fit_A1_heat_mn_f_legacy.rds and cache/fit_A1_heat_mn_f_corrected.rds with positions from the two united tables (04_item6.R).
challenges.result: All confirmed. 287 with q < 0.01 in legacy mode; 157 removed by the filter, 138 of them on NC_001276.1 (all 138 significant mitochondrial CpGs are removed; 363 mitochondrial CpGs tested in legacy mode, none kept), largest difference among the 157 is 12.2 points. All ten CpGs are in the corrected table with identical p-values; q 0.00449 to 0.00943 in legacy mode, 0.01030 to 0.01955 in corrected mode. All 130 retained significant CpGs: 84 still below 0.01. Benjamini-Hochberg: 15 and 4 DML. SLIM q is 0.913 (legacy) and 0.904 (corrected) times the Benjamini-Hochberg q.

challenges.claim: Item 6: 'A CpG at which one group of animals is uniformly different from all others is what an allele or a sequence variant shared by related animals produces in bisulfite data (I-08, I-49).'
challenges.objection: A defender reads the same pattern (methylated only in heat-treated triploids) as the ploidy by heat effect the draft claims.
challenges.test_done: Per-library counts read from both united tables; checked whether the call depends on the correction; no alignments are available, so genotype cannot be called.
challenges.result: Values confirmed (62.5%, 45.8%, 37.5%, 41.7%, 35.5% in the five heat triploids; 6.9% in zr3534_2; 0 of 13 to 31 reads in the 16 others). The dispersion estimate at this CpG is 0.54, so methylKit applied no correction: its 'corrected' p-values (1.8e-17 ploidy, 3.8e-22 heat) are the uncorrected ones. It is not called inside the heat cohort alone (q = 0.06). Whether it is an allele cannot be decided from counts.
challenges.proposed_text: A CpG at which one group of animals is uniformly different from all others is what an allele or a sequence variant shared by related animals produces in bisulfite data (I-08, I-49); it is also what a methylation difference confined to heat-treated triploids would produce, and the counts cannot tell the two apart. At this CpG the dispersion estimate is 0.54, so the correction was not applied and the corrected p-values are the uncorrected ones (item 7).

challenges.claim: Item 7: 'A short corrected list is therefore not evidence that two groups are alike at every CpG. It is evidence that these data cannot name the CpGs at which they differ. Item 2 is the better guide to whether groups differ at all.'
challenges.objection: Fair on power, but it treats the corrected list as a trustworthy lower bound. If the corrected test also calls CpGs for arbitrary groupings, a corrected list is not evidence of difference either.
challenges.test_done: Thresholds recomputed from analyses.csv residual df; t equivalents; corrected calls counted under relabelling at the p threshold of each observed list and at p < 0.01/480,579 (15, 15b).
challenges.result: Thresholds confirmed (84.11, 89.51, 250.61, 474.47; chi-squared 31.42). An F of 84 with 1 and 19 df is a t of 9.2, reached when two groups of 11 lie 3.9 within-group standard deviations apart; for 6 against 6 the figures are 15.8 and 9.1, for 5 against 5 they are 21.8 and 13.8. So the power statement is fair. But relabelled libraries are called too: 22 libraries, median 0 calls, 8 of 200 relabellings with 2 or more, 0.14 per relabelling below 2.1e-8; controls, median 2, 95 of 150 regroupings with 2 or more, 2.2 per regrouping below 2.1e-8; heat cohort, median 10 (5th to 95th percentile 4 to 41, largest 69) against 125 with the real labels, 5.4 per regrouping below 2.1e-8 (3.9 for the 100 groupings two exchanges away). Expected below 2.1e-8 under a test that holds its level: 0.01.
challenges.proposed_text: A short corrected list is therefore not evidence that two groups are alike at every CpG, and a corrected list is not a list of established differences either. These data cannot name the CpGs at which groups differ. Item 2, read against relabelled libraries, is the better guide to whether groups differ at all.

challenges.claim: What follows, Ploidy: 'The 1,038 ploidy DML cannot be reported as differences between diploid and triploid oysters. Lists of that size arise from arbitrary groupings of these animals (item 5), the corrected test finds nearly the p-value distribution of no difference (item 2) [...] This removes the basis of Results 3.2 to 3.5 as far as they concern ploidy'.
challenges.objection: Defender: (1) q < 0.01 with a difference threshold and the default model is the practice of the methylKit vignette; (2) the corrected F test has little power with 11 per group, so 2 survivors prove nothing; (3) pooling two cohorts with a covariate is legitimate; (4) most of the 1,038 are differences inside the heat cohort, where the audit itself says the groups differ.
challenges.test_done: (1) vignette read. (2) corrected p-values at the 1,038 against the CpGs above 20 points of 150 relabellings (11); lists at q < 0.05 and q < 0.1 (13). (3) hybrid labellings and the tested interaction under relabelling. (4) within-cohort pooled differences and within-cohort fits at the 1,038 (13).
challenges.result: (1) True: the vignette calls calculateDiffMeth(meth) with defaults and getMethylDiff(difference = 25, qvalue = 0.01). The text does not say so. (2) Power does not explain it: of the 1,038, 782 (75.3%) have a corrected p below 0.05, 278 (26.8%) below 0.01, 48 (4.6%) below 0.001; relabelled lists give 71.6%, 28.3%, 4.7% on average, and 27, 66, 48 of 150 relabellings give at least the real share. Median dispersion at the 1,038 is 6.57 (relabelled lists 6.16; typical eligible CpG 3.67). With q < 0.05 the corrected test calls 3 ploidy CpGs above 20 points, with q < 0.1 it calls 6. (3) With the heat cohort at its real labels, 903 of 924 regroupings of the controls give at least as long a pooled list; the interaction is beyond relabelling (1 of 300). (4) True and not said in this bullet: 880 of the 1,038 exceed 20 points with the same sign inside the heat cohort, 335 inside the control cohort, 179 in both; 860 are DML of the heat-only fit, 300 of the control-only fit, 139 of both. Of all 751 CpGs that are DML in both within-cohort fits, 139 have the same sign. The conclusion that the list has no support as a list of ploidy loci stands; 'arbitrary groupings' and 'cannot be reported as differences' say more than that.
challenges.proposed_text: - *Ploidy.* The 1,038 ploidy DML cannot be reported as loci that differ between diploid and triploid oysters, in general or "under control conditions". A list of that length cannot be told apart from the lists of relabelled libraries (item 5), with the correction its p-values are those of relabelled libraries (item 2), and the ploidy difference of one cohort is not found in the other (I-01, I-49). What the list mostly holds is the difference between the two ploidy groups of the heat experiment (third point): 860 of the 1,038 are DML among the heat-treated libraries alone and 300 among the controls alone (`dml_counts.csv`, analyses A4, column `n_in_primary`), 139 in both. That difference is real at the level of the groups, but its CpGs cannot be named: of the 125 CpGs called there with the correction, 7 are among the 1,038. Results 3.2 to 3.5 are therefore without support where they present ploidy DML as loci that differ by ploidy: Table 1, Figures 2 to 9 where they show ploidy DML, and the "interaction" set that is built from the ploidy list (I-02). The draft's settings are those of the methylKit vignette (default model, q < 0.01 and a difference threshold), so this is a finding about what common practice gives on these 22 libraries, not about an error of execution.

challenges.claim: What follows, Ploidy inside the heat cohort: 'Diploids and triploids of the heat experiment differ: 12,405 DML uncorrected, 125 corrected, and the number of CpGs above 20 points (13,028) is the largest that any of the 252 relabellings of those ten libraries gives.'
challenges.objection: The count may not single out the ploidy grouping, and '125 corrected' may be read as 125 established loci.
challenges.test_done: permutation_reference.csv and library_methylation_level/relabelling_small_sets.csv; corrected F shares and corrected calls under all 125 other groupings (08, 15); dispersion estimates at the 125 (20).
challenges.result: The group difference stands by three statistics: count above 20 points 13,028 against a median of 4,019.5 (2 of 252, the smallest share possible); corrected F share 17.4% against at most 16.7% in 125 other groupings; 125 corrected calls against at most 69. But the runner-up grouping (zr3534_1 and zr3534_6 exchanged) gives 12,822 CpGs above 20 points, and groupings that keep the three high diploid libraries together give 10% to 13% of corrected p below 0.05. The 125 are not established loci: 124 were tested without the correction (dispersion estimate not above 1; diploids and triploids do not overlap at 124), other groupings give a median of 10 such calls, 122 remain under Benjamini-Hochberg, 7 are among the draft's 1,038, and 101 of the 125 are lower in triploids.
challenges.proposed_text: - *Ploidy inside the heat cohort.* The diploid and the triploid libraries of the heat experiment differ as groups: the number of CpGs above 20 points (13,028) is the largest that any of the 252 relabellings of those ten libraries gives, although the grouping that exchanges zr3534_1 and zr3534_6 gives nearly as many (12,822; `library_methylation_level/relabelling_small_sets.csv`). The two list sizes, 12,405 uncorrected and 125 corrected, do not count established loci: relabelled libraries give a median of 4,019.5 CpGs above 20 points (`permutation_reference.csv`) and about ten corrected calls (item 7), and 124 of the 125 were tested without the correction because their dispersion estimate is not above 1. I-49 describes the difference: three diploid libraries with a higher overall methylation level, and five triploid libraries that resemble each other. Whether heat produced it cannot be decided without WGBS of that experiment's own control animals.

challenges.claim: What follows, Heat: 'The experiments do differ (item 2; I-44), but which CpGs differ cannot be named: 16 CpGs pass with the correction, 6 with the coverage filter.'
challenges.objection: A defender may say 16 named CpGs, or 185 with the chi-squared form, are a list.
challenges.test_done: Stability of the 16 under the filter and under Benjamini-Hochberg (04); corrected p-values at the draft's 2,351 heat DML (13); level of the chi-squared form under relabelling (10) and from the F distribution.
challenges.result: 16, 6, 15 and 4 confirmed. Of the draft's 2,351 heat DML, 82.0% have a corrected p below 0.05, 43.1% below 0.01, 11.9% below 0.001, above the 95th percentile of relabelled ploidy lists (79.7%, 36.6%, 10.1%), which agrees with 'the experiments do differ'. With q < 0.05 the corrected test calls 55 heat CpGs, with q < 0.1 it calls 125. The chi-squared form gives 7.2%, 2.2%, 0.47% under relabelling and is about 1,000 times too liberal at the p needed for a single call, so its 185 are not a list either.

challenges.claim: Options, option 1: 'Make the corrected model primary and report what it supports: no list of ploidy loci, no list of heat loci [...] This is the option the evidence supports.'
challenges.objection: The evidence supports reporting no list; it does not show that methylKit's corrected test is a sound primary analysis. If it were primary, its own lists (2, 16 or 6, 125) would have to be reported at face value.
challenges.test_done: Corrected calls under relabelling and the share of calls made without the correction (14, 15, 15b).
challenges.result: The corrected test leaves the test uncorrected at CpGs with a dispersion estimate not above 1; relabelled libraries get 0.14 (22 libraries), 2.2 (controls) and 5.4 (heat cohort) calls per relabelling below p = 2.1e-8, where 0.01 is expected. The recommendation 'no list' is supported more strongly than the text says; 'make the corrected model primary' is not supported without this caveat.
challenges.proposed_text: 1. Report no list of loci. With variation among animals modelled, these data support no list of ploidy loci and no list of heat loci, and a difference between the ploidy groups of the heat cohort that is described at the level of libraries (I-49). This is the option the evidence supports. The evidence is the relabelling references together with the corrected test; methylKit's corrected test is not by itself a calibrated primary analysis, because it leaves the test uncorrected wherever the dispersion estimate is not above 1 (item 7).

additions.item: The corrected lists are not lists with 1% false discoveries: relabelled libraries are called by the same corrected test, and nearly all calls are made at CpGs where methylKit applied no correction.
